not_exported.detail: Fleet's built-in skills (presentation-builder, svg-builder, mermaid-diagram-builder, generate-skill, fleet-guide and others) ship with Fleet's runtime. The exported agent doesn't have them.

left_behind: Conversations: past threads stay in Fleet. The deployment starts with none.
Traces: the deployment traces to a new LangSmith project. Past traces stay in the Fleet agent's project.
notes: Connections: the sandbox uses your existing `linear` connection to sign in to api.linear.app.
Connections: the sandbox uses your existing `git-host` connection to sign in to git.example.com.

connections.summary: The sandbox signs in to www.googleapis.com with each user's own account. Fleet signed in through its own OAuth app; in MDA you register your own. Each user signs in the first time the agent needs it.
steps: Create the connection. It prints the redirect URI to add to your app: `mda connections create google --oauth google --client-id <client id> --secret-from-env GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET --scope https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.readonly`.

connections.summary: The sandbox signs in to api.acme-crm.dev with each user's own account. Fleet signed in through its own OAuth app; in MDA you register your own. Each user signs in the first time the agent needs it.
steps: Register an OAuth app with the service behind Fleet's `acme-crm-oauth-provider` provider.

Create the connection. It prints the redirect URI to add to your app: `mda connections create acme-crm --authorize-url <authorization URL> --token-url <token URL> --client-id <client id> --secret-from-env ACME_CRM_CLIENT_SECRET`. If `mda connections catalog` lists the service, pass `--oauth <service>` instead of `--authorize-url` and `--token-url`.

connections.summary: The sandbox sends the Fleet workspace secret `ACME_PAIR` to api.acme.dev as Basic auth, through a connection the agent owns. An agent-owned connection can only be created after the deployment exists, so the rules that use it are commented out in `sandbox/__init__.py`.
steps: Put the value of the Fleet workspace secret `ACME_PAIR` in `.env` as `ACME_PAIR`, then create the connection: `mda connections create acme-pair --secret-from-env ACME_PAIR`
In `sandbox/__init__.py`, uncomment the rules that use `acme-pair`.

sandbox: The `Authorization` header Fleet added to requests for api.acme-crm.dev wasn't carried over: MDA sends Basic auth only with a username that is set, has no colon, and isn't the credential itself, and Fleet's username doesn't fit. If api.acme-crm.dev needs it, add the header to the rule in `sandbox/__init__.py` yourself.

The `Authorization` header Fleet added to requests for dev.azure.com wasn't carried over: MDA sends Basic auth only with a username that is set, has no colon, and isn't the credential itself, and Fleet's username doesn't fit. If dev.azure.com needs it, add the header to the rule in `sandbox/__init__.py` yourself.

Requests to api.github.com, github.com won't be signed in to GitHub. Fleet used its own GitHub App for this. To set it up in MDA, run `mda channels init github` and then `mda channels setup`, which creates a GitHub App for this agent. Then add a rule for api.github.com, github.com to `sandbox/__init__.py` that uses `connections.get("mda/github-token", {"type": "agent"})`.

Couldn't read Fleet access profile `p-missing` (it may have been deleted), so its settings couldn't be carried over to `sandbox/__init__.py`. If you still need them, check the profile in Fleet and add them to `sandbox/__init__.py`.

Copied Fleet's sandbox environment variables into `.env` as `SANDBOX_ENV_LOG_LEVEL`. `mda deploy` sends them to the deployment as secrets, and `sandbox/__init__.py` passes each to the sandbox under its Fleet name.
memory: `memory.py` gives the agent its own memory in `memories/agent/`. It starts empty, and the agent adds to it as it learns.
